summary: the measurement error of a measured value against a reference value, and its magnitude

inputs.name: measured
inputs.meaning: the measured quantity value, in the quantity's unit

inputs.name: reference
inputs.meaning: the reference quantity value it is compared with, in the same unit

outputs.name: error
outputs.meaning: the measured value minus the reference value, in the quantity's unit; its sign says on which side of the reference the measured value lies

outputs.name: magnitude
outputs.meaning: the absolute value of the error, in the quantity's unit: what a tolerance in that unit is compared with

validity: two values of one quantity in one unit; it judges nothing: whether the magnitude is small enough is a tolerance a person chooses

source.citation: JCGM 200:2012, International vocabulary of metrology - Basic and general concepts and associated terms (VIM), 3rd edition, 2008 version with minor corrections, BIPM (read 2026-11-17, https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/2071204/JCGM_200_2012.pdf; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261117-jcgm-200-2012-vim)
source.locus: entry 2.16 (3.10), measurement error, printed page 22: the measured quantity value minus a reference quantity value

note: Found by search for where the difference of a measured value and a reference value is defined, for the agreement of a scientific task (meta_agent/failures.jsonl cfd-7, run cfd/20261117-14, tasks/019). The error is the entry's definition; the magnitude is its absolute value, which the entry does not name, and is given because a tolerance in the quantity's unit judges a distance, not a side. No value of the source stands behind the worked cases: each is worked by hand in its worked field. v2 is v1 made common, unchanged in its code and its cases' values: every simulation bundle carries it (the person, 2026-11-18, docs/ideas/20261118.md; meta_agent/tasks/025), and each worked case names the kind of system it is worked on, at least two unrelated kinds. A build adapts it to an engine as a next version that names the engine and says adapted_from.
